n: Despite the miracle, the crowd splits up and drifts away, each going their own way and leaving Nephi standing alone.
Nephi walks home, pondering what the Lord had shown him. Pondering, thinking deeply about sacred things, often comes right before revelation in scripture.
He is discouraged by the people’s secret crimes, murders, and wickedness. While he is pondering in this low moment, the Lord’s voice comes to him.
The Lord blesses Nephi for preaching tirelessly, without fear, not seeking to save his own life but seeking God’s will. God noticed his faithfulness even when no one else listened.

f.w: hast not sought thine own life

n: Because of this, the Lord will make Nephi mighty in word, deed, faith, and works. Whatever Nephi asks will be done, because Nephi will never ask against God’s will. His power rests on complete trust.

f.w: thou shalt not ask that which is contrary to my will

n: “Thou art Nephi, and I am God.” Before His angels, the Lord gives Nephi power to send famine, plague, and destruction according to the people’s wickedness.

f.w: in the presence of mine angels

n: The Lord gives Nephi the sealing power: what he binds or seals on earth will be bound in heaven. Jesus gave the same power to Peter, and Latter-day Saints believe it was restored through Elijah in 1836.

f.w: whatsoever ye shall seal on earth shall be sealed in heaven

n: With this power, if Nephi said a temple would be torn apart, it would happen.
Even mountains would obey him and be leveled, echoing Jesus’s teaching about faith moving mountains.
If Nephi declared that God would strike the people, it would come to pass.
Then the Lord gives a command: go and warn the people that unless they repent, they will be destroyed. The power comes with a mission.
Nephi does not even finish going home. He turns around at once and goes back to the scattered crowds to deliver the Lord’s warning. His obedience is immediate.

f.w: did not go unto his own house

n: Even after the miracle about the chief judge, the people harden their hearts and refuse to listen.
Nephi delivers the message plainly: repent or be destroyed.
They still refuse, insult him, and try to arrest him.
But God’s power protects him. The Spirit carries him away from among them so they cannot seize him.
By the Spirit, Nephi goes from crowd to crowd until everyone has heard God’s word, directly or through his messengers.
They still won’t listen. Contention grows until they turn on each other with the sword, a civil war.
So ends the seventy-first year of the judges, about 21 BC.
